Very good old school mmo. Tons of skills and classes to play and alot of unique concepts added. Its something you can sink many hours into... not really a negative but there are so many options of things to do you can get lost easily. I start off a day focusing on cooking then I find a mat I need for shamanic infusion... which leads to... etc etc.

The negatives... In a word, GRAPHICS. While it isnt bad, it isnt what would be called peak by todays standards...well old school and all of that.. Also there is a bit of jank with the combat and minor issues like pulling mobs thru walls and such. 

Overall a great game if you want to waste your time being entertained. There is ALWAYS something to do.

Project Gorgon isn't for everyone, sometimes I question if it's even for me, but then I find another thing that grabs my attention and I lose hours of the day into it. 

It's like Runescape + Morrowind, which sounds amazing on paper but in practice it's pretty janky sometimes. Floaty movement, sometimes awkward tab targeting from line-of-sight issues, and just some inexplicable odd behaviour is to be expected. Gameplay takes some getting used to and without taking some time to customize your controls you're gonna have a harder time.

Lots of time spent reading in-game and in the wiki to understand systems and mechanics that ocassionally feel overcomplicated to a fault. Not really an issue for this type of game, just know what you're getting into. The /wiki "thing" command is extremely useful. Price checking items is still annoying though, for the love of god please let the Shop Tracking Golems show prices so I don't need to go between zones just to see the price of something.

Some zones need a lot of optimization work; weather effects like rain and especially the snowing areas give me massive performance drops. Surprising this is an issue given the graphic style. I don't feel like this should be the type of game to require endlessly tweaking graphic settings with my specs.

I've not paid much or any attention to the main story, but the game experience and journey itself is what is compelling to me.

Overall, this is a love it or really hate it type of game.

Pros, Cons, Review: (points in no specific order)
[b]Pros:[/b]

- the game offers unusual experiences and allows players to play their own way. There are no classes, only skills and abilities that can be raised.
- the game is quiet and mostly friendly. 
- huge solo player content
- no idiot markers (I personally find that harmonious)

[b]Cons:[/b] 

- the game returns to "the roots" of MMO and picks up mechanics which were awful  then and are still awful now. (Low lv mobs still aggro, mob "trains", griefing, loot issues, extremely limited player travel skips (teleports), basically all the bad stuff that got ditched for good reasons)
- real player mods, which is also a real bad idea (and they can act with total impunity)
- no instancing, meaning lvl 80 players will come clean out lvl 20 dungeons for loot and you will either die in the process and lose progress or left with nothing for 30 min. 
- this is esp bad when you are near a boss, you *will* be put on their aggro table without even touching them, the boss will die, get looted and you will be locked out from killing it for loot for 3h
- really bad market system that bottlenecks progress and fosters monopolies in a few player's hands
- the resource management is unrefined and also leads to massive bottlenecks to waste your time or favour players who are advanced enough to basically "own" the entire map, leaving you with scraps
- outpoken, rampant racism. Sexism and tiresome tropes and stereotyping are part of 80% of the npcs and thus a constant presence, not an exception. And it gets very crass at times.

[b]Review:[/b]

The game feels like 1990s in many ways, good and bad. Still I can't help but think that the creator is stuck trying to reimagine a nostalgic figment to satisfy their own needs while clearly showing the neglect for the group they need (and very much hate) the most: the players.
There no good way to describe the game other than being spiteful in detail. While the overall appeal is peaceful and respects your playstyle especially if you do things on your own and in your own mind, you must either condone or blinker the rest (and that rest is the disgusting stuff). 
I will say that this is on purpose. The game is deliberately offensive in a childish way, a petulant way and a cruel way, and it is so because it wants to alienate and upset certain people groups. It is hedging the turf for those who despite all that create their own little bubbles, and who may be good people under that hateful barb wire offering seclusion. But it changes nothing about the fact that this toxic trash is part of the game.

Either way, the dev wants to feel like the old, tough veteran who is better than others, and his old and tired ideas are sarcosanct.

I will admit I enjoyed that, because I too am old. But ♥♥♥♥, you gotta go with the times or be left behind.

And that is my suggestion. Leave that game behind.

I enjoyed the game at first. Being in the MMO drought that we have right now, I was looking forward to a new world to explore. I liked the concept of learning as you do and not being restricted by a class.

Unfortunately, they have so many artificial and dumb systems to slow down players.
Merchants have a weekly cash limits and not all merchants buy everything (which is super annoying). You have two options; You grind reputation with the merchants to increase the amount available every week or you go all around the different maps to find different vendors. So you end up dropping on the ground most of the loot you find.
And having to go to 10 different vendors to empty your inventory is so annoying. What a dumb system. I understand the idea but in practice, it's not good.
Also, limiting people's ability to sell by putting a weekly limit is the worst idea possible. Reduce the price of each individual items but remove the limit. Making people throw away their loot isn't a good game design.

Crafting is also tedious. I like slow systems but, as an example, if you reach lvl 20 in animal handling, you need a string, which should be an easy item to acquire. You can craft it by reaching lvl 12 in tailoring (forgot the in game skill name). To reach lvl 12 in tailoring, you need a boat load of cotton. To get cotton, you need to run around the map, looking for the occasional plant (each harvest give 1 cotton and you need 4 cotton for the basic level 1 recipe). My example doesn't reflect well how tedious it is but that was just because I wanted to tame the second type of pets.

So to craft, you need lots of items. When you explore, you get lots of items. It would be good if you could store it.. But wait... you can't!! You have limited storage that is mostly link to each settlement. There's also a dynamic storage where the community can pay for slots but they cost a fortune. So as a new player, you can't contribute. I came back to the game after a few days and the dynamic storage was at -9 slots. So I either had to remove items or leave them there and lock myself out of the biggest storage (which is about 20-30 storage slots). There's maybe 3-4 other individual storage in the ''first city'' but they have about 10 slots each. That seems like a lot but to give an example, you don't have passive healing, you need to eat food to get healing buff. To craft food, you often need about 3+ different items for the basic food. All that just to say that the storage is faaar from being enough just to store crafting components.

Also, performance  can be really bad in some zone in the map. For instances regions with such bad graphic, it doesn't make sense. They have bad coding.

This game is an absolute masterpiece for a certain type of person. It's unlike anything else out there, and it can absolutely be janky and weird - but it's also amazing in part because of that jank and weirdness. Most of the negative comments seem to come from people that don't really get what type of game it's supposed to be, it's not the normal "treadmill progression" seen on other MMOs. It can largely be played solo or group. Builds aren't perfectly "balanced" but they're all useful. There's no "bricking" of a build, you can simply start leveling up other skills if you don't like what you picked. Some of the complaints here just seem odd - unarmed works fine with wolf form, and in fact it's pretty popular among people who play wolves. As for developer (or really any) drama, I've never experienced any - the community is fun and more helpful than any other I've ever experienced.

I've played a long time ago on the main server before the game officially was "released" and I came back recently to play again on a new server and it's been a blast. The magic of the game quickly came back - people asking for help and being invited to guilds, people offering helpful advice on the 'help' channel, and the starting experience truly open ended in a way few games are. It's not a "fast" experience - it's a slow marathon of a game, not a sprint. If you're the type of player to immediately ask what end game is like, you might not be the right fit. If you're the type of player that believes a $30 game that provides *hundreds* of hours - even some of the negative reviews have *hundreds* of hours played on this game - of entertainment... then you'll definitely feel like you've gotten your money's worth. I do, and I haven't experienced nearly everything the game has to offer. Right now, in 2026, this is the one MMO I feel has some of the magic of discovery and the early EverQuest days, or WoW-when-it-first-came-out feeling. It's fun, it's sometimes frustrating, but people are always willing to help. Hands down the best community of peeps in any MMO I've ever played in, and that includes the older games. The player base skews more adult in this game, which I think can be a good thing!

If you're burned out on MMOs there's absolutely no reason not to try this game. It's pretty neat and it's a game that couldn't ever be put out by a "big studio" - it has a charm all of its own. Highly recommend.

There are systems in the game that makes sense for them to exist, but they ultimately feel unfinished, overall making the game feel like it's having and identity crisis. In my opinion, if the developers were to focus one aspect of the game at a time and completely flesh it out before adding or moving onto another system, then maybe I would feel as if this game worth sticking with, but if they continue with this method of development, I do not see the game lasting till it's full release. With this in mind I cannot currently recommend the game if you are looking to spend a lot of time diving deep into leveling it's systems. As it stands right now, it seems as if the community and it's events is what is keeping the game afloat.

I really enjoyed this game when it first launched. Played right up until the beginning of May. Great community and concept. But while a lot of the concepts are absolutely amazing, the general execution is very amateurish and unprofessional. 

Sadly, I don't agree with the development team at all. Their scope is very skewed and when you watch interviews made in the past, it all starts to make sense. There is a real feeling of omnipotence between the staff and the players. If you as a player make a mistake, they are quick to gag or punish you. If an admin makes a mistake, the creator of the project will write a heartfelt apology towards said admin. There is no real accountability for wrongdoings, and in true indie fashion, the staff team is very toxic.

There's no question about Citan's abilities, but beware that he's got his own idea of things and his own schedule he works on. He is adamant against merges, yet I've seen my server (Strekios) lose more than half of it's original population. All of my friends have quit, all of the faces I came to recognise have vanished. I used to find a group to do casino dailies within 15 minutes. 

Now I need to consecutively log on for hours, spam global chat and pray I find a group. Plus given he would rather defend an abusive admin than formally apologise to the players. Sure, he made an announcement about it, but more than half of his apology was towards the admin, not the players.

There's that, and then his new scope: localisation. He's been working quite actively on this, to his credit, but for a game that is rapidly dying, instead of fixing the barren Rahu or Ilmari Desert, fixing the numerous of bugs or performance, this seems like a very bad scope.

There is also no endgame other than zergs and while there are some endgame dungeons and activities, these are really deserved for min maxers. Prodigy is an impossible grind (a minimum of 3 weeks or more, doing timegated dailies). Re-rolling and re-leveling a combat skill takes you through the same dated content that has been in the game for a decade (Serbule Crypt for example). 

The casino shop update was another weird scope. A quarter or even half of the stalls in Serbule are now empty on Strekios, and there is maybe one shop in the casino. It really makes me wonder what was the point of opening a gigantic shopping mall in the casino to begin with - the resources could have been spent on something more important.

I made a guild and we grinded to unlock the guild hall. Placing items on the walls bugs them through the roof, and every time the instance resets, the items are moved and misaligned. There is also no real goal to do anything there other than putting down a roster or whatever. The barber shop or whatever is planned in Serbule has also been a 'work in progress' for far too long...

I still recommend people to try it out, but don't buy it full price and expect the content to try up around 200 hours. Don't hope for any steady or meaningful updates, because the dev team has imaginary data that they prioritise at will without really taking the community's concerns into account.. Wait for a discount or play the demo first, since this game has a steep learning curve and no hand holding at all. The wiki is also still unfinished, even after a decade of contributions, a lot of the pages are just exports made from the cdn with no real direction on where to go. 

Good for a few hundred hours if you get past the learning curve, so in that sense, it might be worth your money. But not an MMO that encourages player longevity.

I started playing this game on the demo in late april/early may 2026 which is later than a lot of the other reviews. I saw a video about it and was looking for something to play once Monsters&Memories launch was delayed by 5 months. I played the demo for about 10 hours because it allows you to get any skill to level 15 and your account transfers over once you buy the game. Overall I think it's worth playing and I've enjoyed it. I don't know how to organize a review so I'll just list positives and negatives.

Positives: 
It's like runescape where you don't have a class but instead can do all of the skills on one character. This allows you to reroll if you're not enjoying the class you're playing. There is also a synergy system where for example I got to gardening level 45 and it granted me 1 pig level. This isn't important early on but is pretty significant at higher levels. Basically the game encourages you to do a variety of things. 

There is also this Ed, Edd & Eddy "chasing the jawbreaker" feeling some games do well and Project Gorgan kind of nailed it. You end up having intertwined goals that you need to complete in order to move forward, "I must do X so that I can do Y so that I can do Z". For example I wanted to unlock the priest skill but to do so I needed compassion or psychology at level 25 first. Then I needed to increase reputation with the trainer so that she would teach me. One of her favorite gifts was a gem called lapis lazule which you can get from surveying blue gems, but I needed a level 15 surveying skill to do so. But then I needed to become friends with the surveying lady in order to unlock it. I had all of these fulfilling mini grinds to do in order to unlock the combat skill I wanted to try out. You finally achieve your goal and get hit with that feeling from the WoW episode of southpark where he goes "What do you mean? Now we can finally play the game". 

The community is also pretty cozy. If you say you are a new player people get excited and tell you welcome. People like answering questions in the help channel, I asked how to join a guild and someone invited me to theirs. People kind of hang out in town and play music and it reminds me how mmorpgs felt before dungeon queues. I haven't had negative interactions yet. 

There are just so many skills. You can look up the project gorgon wiki and they're all listed on the front. There are animal skills too, some of them are dps or support or tank. There are lots of different builds to work with since you use 2 combat skills and have separate action bars for them. I've rerolled 4 times, first as a sword/psychologist from tutorial island to an unarmed/animal handler to a fire magic/priest to now a pig/mentalist. There are also a ton of crafting/misc skills. There is even a skill for dying and one called Gourmand that is levelled up by each unique food item you eat. You'll always have something to work on and level up and it's all on one character. 

The world is just very silly and nice to look at. The tutorial island was kind of depressing feeling but it felt really bright once I got to serbule. The dialogues have a lot of soul and humor in them. You can tell the maker of the game really cared about it. 
 
Negatives: 

At the point I joined the game most of the community had reached level 50+ with their combat skills and so most low level dungeons were not bustling like in the review videos I saw. I started on Dreva which is the first server that came out on launch, there are 3 other launch servers. If I did not have my friend playing with me I would have done all of those alone. I've met a stranger in a dungeon wanting to group up twice in about 120 hours of gameplay. You can easily get a high level to come help you, especially if you join a guild, but it's not the same as tackling a boss with people your own level. You start to get more into group content once you're 50+ in your combat skills. You'll see a lot more of the community hanging around the casino than in the starting cities. It would have been a lot different if I had played at launch and this does make it feel kind of lonely sometimes. On the bright side you don't have to fight for resources like the earlier players did. Still I hope the launch servers get merged some day.

I like diversity in armor and a lot of pieces you pick up will have the same model as something you saw 20 levels ago. For example the yeti moss gear I found in the yeti cave at level 40 was the same model as the spider web gear I found in the crypt at level 20, except with a different color. Though this game was 25$ with no monthly fee and was made by a very small team so I don't blame them. Still I really like seeing a huge variety in models for armor so it's a slight bummer. To compare it to runescape again a lot of the armor in project gorgon is like bronze to rune changing colors but being the same model. 

Summary: 

I think the game is worth trying and is affordable. I'm having a lot of fun still. If you enjoyed levelling up a variety of skills in runescape you would enjoy this game.

This is a wonderful game for people who like having A LOT of different things to do, and especially if you enjoy being a bit lost in it all and figuring things out.  It is not an Endgame loop MMO.  You don't "rush to 100+ to play the REAL game".  It's a journey.

For combat, you pick two skill groups out of the 30+ available to be your active skills.  Those skillsets give you a pool of abilities to assign to your 12 hotbar slots.  Those 12 slots make up your build, and can get surprisingly customized.  Be a Pig/Priest, an Ice/Knife, a Staff/Shield, a Spider/Druid and so on!  I began as a Sword/Psychology character slashing skeletons and insulting their mothers to death.  Then weeks into my journey I unlocked Priest, so I changed to Sword/Priest which let me change many of my slashing attacks into fire damage, and began smiting orcs and bears with holy fire.  I made it to the maximum level available and thought I'd like to try a different spin on Priest, so I leveled up Mentalism - Now I deal emotional damage to these heathens and it's awesome.  Your character can do it all, and switching skillsets just requires being out of combat it's simple.  Want to be a Lycan/Vampire? Go nuts!

There are nearly 50 crafting skills (Fletching, Alchemy, Candlemaking, Brewing etc) to master if you want, and another 50 or so other characters skills (Calligraphy, Goblinese, Meditation, Racing etc) that you might find interesting as well.  They interweave with each other at various points, making specialized crafters a large part of a healthy community.  

Just about everyone in Project Gorgon is on a completely different path from one another, and it meshes into a fun chaos where your skill choices are always playable, your crafting involvement is always optional, and interacting with your community is largely beneficial.  The world is fun, the zones are unique, and it's just so interesting to see  what details there are around the game.

If you like Indie developed games with a lot of care, silliness, imperfections, options, community, and active development you're going to like this game.  If you like MMOs to blitz through content, reach "endgame", burn out and complain then this is absolutely not the game for you.  If you can keep FOMO in check and socialize with other video game enjoyers you should have a fantastic time with Project Gorgon.

Feel free to check out the demo, or take a leap of faith.  I can only speak to the Dreva server, but I find helpful people in global chat all day long running groups, doing favors, crafting, and having laughs.  10/10 for what this game is trying to be.

TLDR: Aside from all the other complaints in different reviews about the (lack of) balance and poor community moderation, the game is also UNFINISHED and BROKEN. Definitely not ready for release, does not deserve a 1.0 version number. Some issues that can be found reported years ago still remain.

Some examples...

The main story quest line is incomplete. If you get far enough, you're eventually given a quest with the literal title "Wait Until The Next Major Update". The objective of the quest is "Wait patiently" with the promise of "More coming soon".

Broken monster pathfinding that leads to invincible monsters.
Certain monsters in the game have mechanics that break their own pathfinding, like knockback and kick that will make the player leave the ground and jump through the air. When the monster can't find a path to it's target because the target is not on the ground, it's health is reset to 100% but it doesn't disengage from combat, it keeps attacking. Rinse, repeat.

Monsters that constantly disengage and reset.
There are locations in the game where monsters will engage the player, attack, and then run away while resetting their health to full. Then they immediately re-engage, attack, and repeat the cycle. If you're lucky, this is a nuisance that leads to un-defeatable monsters. If you're unlucky, they run away into packs of other monsters that follow them back and swarm the player.

Mouse cursor constantly resets.
Using the mouse to pan the camera around resets it's position to the center of the screen, leading to miss-clicks and missed-clicks. This isn't just annoying, it causes all kinds of unintended interactions with the UI that can be costly either via wasted consumables in the inventory, or failed combat.

Pet logic doesn't work as stated.
Combat pets are a popular choice in the game, but their attack and defense logic doesn't work right. "Assist" mode is supposed to have the pet attack the same target as the player, but the pet will often stay fixated on it's own target. This makes it difficult to impossible to have the pet switch targets when new threats arise that should be prioritized. "Follow" mode is supposed to force the pet to ignore all threats and just follow the player, which is often necessary to use to prevent pets from chasing after targets that have disengaged (see above). But sometimes after putting the pet back on assist, the pet will chase after their previous target, abandoning the player and often attracting swarms of monsters.

The UI is a hot mess.
While not broken per-se, the UI itself is difficult to use and creates gameplay issues. Targeting players and pets for healing is difficult, setting pet attack/defend mode requires clicking very small icons, misclicks are common due to the cursor resetting and the actions are not bindable to keys. In-game chat channels are filtered into different tabs, but messaging is "sticky" - which often results in messages being sent to a different channel than the one currently being read by the player. Re-whispering players with messages intended for guild or global chat is common. Even worse, accidentally broadcasting messages to public channels that were intended to be private whispers, party or guild messages is also common.

Careful giving up your money for this one.
